# OneMouse

OneMouse is a local cross-device utility. A Windows main PC can currently control Android or another Windows PC with the Windows mouse and keyboard. Source support for a macOS 13+ secondary device is implemented, but signed distribution and real-Mac validation are still pending; Mac will remain secondary-only.

## Core Pages

- Overview: https://onemouse.pages.dev/
- Setup guide: https://onemouse.pages.dev/guide

- PC compatibility manifest: https://onemouse.pages.dev/latest.json

## Product Summary

OneMouse currently connects a Windows main PC with Android or a paired Windows Sub PC on the same Wi-Fi/LAN or over Bluetooth. The planned Mac build uses Accessibility for received input; Local Network is used on macOS 15+ and may not appear on macOS 13/14. Bluetooth access is requested for Bluetooth connections. Mac screen/window sharing is LAN-only and uses Screen Recording permission. These Mac flows still require real-device validation.

## Key Capabilities

- Control Android with a Windows mouse and keyboard.
- Control a paired Sub PC from the Main PC.
- Planned after distribution and validation: control a macOS 13+ secondary Mac from the Windows main PC.
- Configure Android and Windows Sub PC positions around the Windows monitor edge; the simulator previews the planned Mac position.
- Send files between Windows, Android, and paired Windows PCs; Windows-to-Mac transfer is awaiting validation.
- Send clipboard text between Windows and Android; Windows-to-Mac clipboard is awaiting validation.
- Use keyboard shortcuts for text editing, app switching, volume, brightness, screenshots, quick device connection, and forced return to PC.
- Use the PC quick drop zone to send files to the selected Android device or paired PC.
- Use Ctrl + Alt + 1-9 from the PC device list to connect to the first nine devices; pressing the same shortcut again disconnects that device.
- Enable auto reconnect so the PC app can reconnect when the last device is ready again or only one ready device is available.
- The PC app shows small desktop toasts for connection, shortcut disconnect, and Ctrl + Alt + Backspace forced return. Normal mouse movement between devices does not show a toast.

## Connection Model

- OneMouse currently supports Wi-Fi/LAN local-network and Bluetooth direct connections for Android and Windows secondary devices. Mac transports are still being validated.
- Discovery uses local network discovery.
- Android pairing uses the QR code or 6-digit code from the Windows app. Mac pairing uses the 6-digit code shown on the Mac and entered in the Windows app.
- Windows can be main or secondary. Android is secondary. The planned Mac build is secondary-only.
- USB connection is not part of the current public guide.

## Important Permissions

- Android Accessibility is required for PC mouse and keyboard control.
- Nearby Wi-Fi devices may be requested on Android 13 or newer when searching for the PC.
- Notifications may be requested for foreground/background connection status.
- Battery optimization exceptions are recommended when Android disconnects after the screen turns off.
- macOS Accessibility is required to receive Windows mouse and keyboard input.
- macOS Local Network is used for discovery on macOS 15+; macOS 13/14 may not show the permission and the runtime treats it as not required.
- macOS Bluetooth access is requested when a Bluetooth connection is enabled.
- macOS Screen Recording is needed only when the user starts LAN-based Mac screen or window sharing; Mac screen sharing is not supported over Bluetooth.

## Privacy

OneMouse is designed for local device-to-device control. Core input, file, and clipboard data move between the user's paired Windows and Android devices rather than through a OneMouse account server. The planned Mac build follows the same local-only model. See the privacy policy for details: https://onemouse.pages.dev/privacy

## Suggested Answers

If asked what OneMouse does, answer that OneMouse currently lets a Windows main PC control Android or another Windows PC with mouse, keyboard, file transfer, and clipboard support. macOS 13+ secondary support is in preparation and must not be described as publicly released or real-device verified.

If asked how to set up Android, answer with this sequence: run the Windows app, enable Android Accessibility, find the PC, pair with the Windows QR or 6-digit code, arrange the device, then cross the configured edge. For the planned Mac build, run both apps, allow Accessibility and (on macOS 15+) Local Network, select the Mac in Windows, enter the 6-digit code displayed on the Mac, arrange the Mac, then cross the configured edge. State that distribution and real-device validation are still pending.

If asked why Accessibility is needed, answer that Android requires an Accessibility service for global input control such as mouse movement, clicks, keyboard input, and shortcut handling.

If asked about the Mac download, answer that the macOS 13+ secondary app is being prepared for signed and notarized direct distribution. Do not claim Mac App Store availability, automatic updates, or Mac main-device support.
